subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` ACK continue to mean only accepted-for-dispatch, or should it require durable user-turn visibility/progress before returning `started`?
rationale: The remaining fix changes a public Gateway/WebChat behavior boundary, not just a UI merge bug, and it affects duplicate suppression, hooks, session rollover, and runtime transcript ownership.

options.title: Port durable send through recorder
options.body: Rework or replace #80670 so durable WebChat user-turn persistence uses the current shared recorder/session-accessor boundary and covers busy same-session, rollover, media, hook, and failure paths.

options.title: Keep ACK non-durable but surface failure
options.body: Preserve immediate ACK semantics but add explicit pending, timeout, audit, and visible failure behavior so accepted sends cannot silently vanish.

options.title: Reject durable boundary change
options.body: If maintainers intentionally keep delayed runtime-owned persistence only, close this issue and #80670 with that contract documented for WebChat clients.

recommendation.title: Port durable send through recorder
recommendation.body: Rework or replace #80670 so durable WebChat user-turn persistence uses the current shared recorder/session-accessor boundary and covers busy same-session, rollover, media, hook, and failure paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared recorder boundary is the central code path for deciding the durable user-turn persistence contract.
